### *** THIS JOB IS ONLY AVAILABLE TO INDIVIDUALS LIVING IN INDIA. NO RECRUITERS OR AGENCIES, PLEASE.***

**About AssetIntel**

AssetIntel is a software company that develops asset management software products for the transportation infrastructure industry. Our clients include state transportation agencies, city governments, toll authorities, transit agencies, the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA), and civil engineering firms. For more information, visit our website.


**Job Description**

We're looking for a Python developer to own the analytical engines behind our products — the codebases where math meets production software. These systems span a range of problems: long-term deterioration modeling and budget optimization, real-time hazard prediction using live data, probabilistic damage assessment, geospatial analysis, and lifecycle cost forecasting. They are the core of what makes our products work.

You'll work alongside domain experts and researchers to turn mathematical formulations into clean, maintainable, production-grade Python. You'll also progressively improve existing code — better architecture, better patterns, better reliability.

This is not a role where you can treat the math as a black box. You need to be genuinely curious about the models and algorithms you're implementing. You don't need to arrive knowing this domain, but you need to be the kind of person who wants to understand it deeply.


**What You'll Do**

* Translate mathematical specifications into production code. You'll receive formulations, equations, and pseudocode from the research side of the team. Your job is to understand the intent and write Python that is correct, readable, testable, and maintainable.
* Improve existing codebases. The current code works in production but has room for architectural improvement. You'll progressively modernize it — better modularity, type safety, test coverage, error handling, and overall code quality.
* Build new analytical features end-to-end. As our products evolve, you'll implement new capabilities — taking them from mathematical concept to deployed, production-ready code.
* Bridge the gap between research and engineering. The ability to communicate across these worlds — asking good questions, translating between math and code, pushing back constructively — will be critical to your success here.


**What We're Looking For**

* At least 3 years of professional experience working with Python.
* Strong Python fundamentals — you write clean, idiomatic Python and care about code quality.
* Experience with numerical/scientific Python libraries: pandas, NumPy, SciPy.
* Ability to read and reason about mathematical formulations — comfort with equations, probability distributions, and optimization concepts, or a genuine eagerness to learn.
* Experience writing and maintaining production Python code, not just scripts or notebooks.
* Good instincts for software architecture — when to refactor, how to decompose large modules, how to manage dependencies.
* Clear communication skills, especially the ability to collaborate with researchers and domain experts.
* Comfort with Git and collaborative development workflows.
* Bonus points if you've worked with any of the following: mathematical optimization (LP, MIP), geospatial tools like GeoPandas or Shapely, real-time data pipelines or external APIs, Docker and containerized deployments, or cloud infrastructure (Azure or similar). We also especially value people who've introduced engineering discipline — tests, CI/CD, type hints — into messy research codebases without breaking everything in the process.


**Nice-to-haves:**

* Experience with multiprocessing in Python and memory-aware resource management.
* Familiarity with probabilistic modeling, fragility analysis, or statistical risk assessment.


**Benefits and Perks**

* Work remotely - anywhere from India.
* Market-competitive total compensation package and performance-based bonus.
* Company-paid medical coverage.
* Fully equipped home office setup, including a high-spec computer, dual monitors, desk, and chair.
* Plenty of growth opportunities, working alongside some of the brightest minds in the industry.

- Build bulletproof API integrations with third-party APIs for various use cases
- Evolve our Infrastructure and add a few more nines to our overall availability

## **About the role:**

More and more developers don't read our docs or click through our dashboard. Their coding agent does. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others are now how a big share of engineers discover, integrate and debug AssemblyAI. We've spent years polishing the human experience. The agent experience (AX) is newer, growing fast, and almost untouched.

That's the job. You'll own how AI agents build with AssemblyAI: the skills, prompts, MCP server, code samples, docs and integrations an agent reads and runs when a developer says "add transcription to my app." Your north star is simple: an agent should go from zero to a working, production-grade AssemblyAI integration on the first try.

You'll work closely with senior engineers on our Product Engineering team, with real ownership from day one and room to grow into leading AX as the area scales.

## **What You’ll Do:**

- **Drive the agent experience.** Treat coding agents as a first-class user of AssemblyAI, alongside the humans who use our dashboard and Playground.
- **Build and maintain agent skills.** Ship skills for our core products (Speech-to-Text, Real-time, Dictation, Voice Agents, TTS, LLM Gateway) that teach agents how to integrate us correctly.
- Build o**n our MCP server and agent integrations.** Extend the AssemblyAI MCP server, help ship agent and MCP auth (OAuth and API keys), and make it easy to plug into Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and whatever comes next.
- **Make our docs and code samples agent-ready.** Own llms.txt, machine-readable docs, quickstarts and SDK examples so agents pick the right API, parameters and patterns the first time.
- **Tune the prompts and instructions behind our product.** Improve the system prompts, tool definitions and agent instructions that power our in-dashboard agent and onboarding flows.
- **Measure it.** Build evals and benchmarks that run real coding agents against real integration tasks. Track success rate, time to first working call, and activation from agent-driven signups.
- **Help us scale the playbook.** Start with one product and then roll what works across every product.
- **Use AI tools as a core part of how you work,** and help the rest of engineering build faster with agents.

## **What You’ll Need:**

- 2+ years of professional software engineering experience, with solid full-stack fundamentals (Javascript and/or Python).
- Daily, hands-on use of coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex, and real curiosity about what makes them succeed or fail.
- Some hands-on experience writing prompts, skills, tool definitions or agent instructions, at work or side projects, and an interest in measuring them with evals rather than vibes.
- Product sense for developer-facing work. You care whether the developer, or their agent, actually gets to a working integration.
- Clear technical writing. Much of this role is writing that agents and humans both read.
- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias to ship. AX is a new discipline, and you'll learn it and help define it alongside us.

## **Nice to Have:**

- Working knowledge of MCP, LLM tool calling, and how agents read docs and APIs.
- You've built or contributed to an MCP server, agent skill library, or coding agent plugin.
- Developer relations, docs engineering, or SDK experience at an API-first company.
- Experience with Voice AI, speech-to-text, or LLM APIs.
- You've shipped something that agents use in the wild, and can show us the before and after.

**Pay Transparency:**

AssemblyAI strives to recruit and retain exceptional talent from diverse backgrounds while ensuring pay equity for our team. Our salary ranges are based on paying competitively for our size, stage, and industry, and are one part of many compensation, benefit, and other reward opportunities we provide.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level, qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.

The provided ranges are the expected salaries for candidates in the United States (USD) and Canada (CAD). Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range which will be communicated to candidates throughout the interview process.

USD Salary Range: $160,000 - $210,000

CAD Salary Range: C$225,000 - C$285,000

We're hiring our first **Senior GTM AI Engineer**. This is a software engineering job inside the revenue org. You will build the pipelines, internal tools, and agents that decide which companies we go after, how we reach them, and what our sellers see when they open their laptop in the morning.

Most of what a sales ops team used to do by hand is now something you can write software to do. Finding every company building voice AI before they contact us. Researching an account and drafting the first email. Watching product usage and telling an AE when a customer is about to expand or churn. Keeping the CRM clean without anyone filling in forms. You will build those systems, run them in production, and be judged on whether pipeline and revenue move.

Your users are our AEs, SDRs, and GTM leaders. Your job is to make a small team perform like one three times its size.

## **What You'll Do**

- Write code every day. Python services, SQL models, scheduled jobs, and small internal apps are most of the job. You'll use Claude Code and similar tools to ship in days what used to take a quarter.
- Build agents that do the work: account research, lead qualification, outreach drafting, CRM hygiene, and usage monitoring. Design them, give them tools and data, evaluate their output, and keep them running.
- Turn product usage data in BigQuery and Looker into signals sellers act on: usage alerts, expansion triggers, and account health scores.
- Build the account targeting machine: sourcing, enrichment, dedupe, and ICP scoring, from raw data to a ranked list in a rep's queue.
- Integrate the systems the team already uses (our CRM, enrichment providers, outbound tools) so data moves between them without a human in the loop.
- Keep funnel data trustworthy: routing rules, field governance, and attribution.
- Prototype fast, measure what works, kill what doesn't, and work directly with Sales and Marketing leadership on what to build next.
- Document what you build so it keeps running without you.

## **What You'll Need**

- 4+ years as a software engineer, data engineer, or growth/GTM engineer, with time spent shipping systems that other people depend on.
- Strong Python and SQL. You have owned production automations end to end: APIs, webhooks, scheduled jobs, retries, error handling, and monitoring.
- Experience building with LLMs beyond a single prompt: multi-step agents, tool use, retrieval, and evaluation. You can tell whether an agent's output is good, and you know when a plain script is the better tool.
- AI-assisted development is how you work. You use Claude Code or similar tools daily, and you have the engineering judgment to review, test, and stand behind what they produce.
- Solid fundamentals: clean code, version control, code review, debugging, and a habit of thinking in systems. You do not need an engineering team to ship.
- Curiosity about how a sales org works. You don't need a RevOps background, but you need to care about how deals get found and closed, and be willing to learn our CRM and the tools around it quickly.
- A builder's mindset with an operator's judgment: you scope for business impact, ship iteratively, and measure results in pipeline and revenue.
- Low ego, high ownership, and comfort being the single-threaded owner of an entire domain.

## **Nice to Have**

- Hands-on Salesforce or other CRM work at the object and API level, or experience with enrichment and outbound tools like Clay.
- dbt, BigQuery, and Looker, or an equivalent warehouse and BI stack.
- Time at a developer-facing or API-first company, or selling to technical buyers.
- You've been the first engineer in a sales or growth org and built the function from scratch.

**About Bitwarden**

Bitwarden is the trusted identity security leader for millions of users worldwide, empowering enterprises, developers, and individuals to securely manage and share sensitive information anywhere. Bitwarden makes it easy for all users to extend robust security across their devices with password management, secrets management, and passwordless and passkey innovations. The company is headquartered in Santa Barbara, California with team members located across the globe. Learn more at [_bitwarden.com_](https://bitwarden.com/). 

**The Role**

As a Senior Software Engineer on Bitwarden's Secrets Manager team, you will build and operate the application stack that lets developers, DevOps, and cybersecurity teams centrally store, manage, and deploy sensitive credentials. This is a **hands-on role**. You will spend your time writing, reviewing, and shipping code within core concepts of secrets, projects, machine accounts, and access tokens across the product suite.

Secrets Manager spans a .***NET API, a Rust SDK core, and a TypeScript and Angular web client,*** with SDK bindings in eight further languages and integrations written in Go, C++, Java, PHP and Python. You should be comfortable moving between languages and learning new ones as the work demands, developing deep expertise as you go.

#### **WHAT YOU WILL DO**

- **End-to-End Delivery & Ownership:** Own features from specification through production. Write the design, build it across the API, client, and SDK, test it, ship it, and stay with it once it is live.
- **Engineering Standards and Automated Quality:** Review your teammates' pull requests with care and invite the same scrutiny of your own. Pair on hard problems, share what you learn, and help newer engineers find their footing in a security-sensitive codebase.
- **Decoupled Architecture and Service Boundaries:** Maintain clean service boundaries and design resilient APIs so Secrets Manager can evolve independently of the core platform.
- **Deep Technical Work & Codebase Health:** Take on the hardest problems in the codebase. Contribute to performance, reliability, accessibility, architecture and maintainability.
- **AI-Assisted Development:** Use AI coding assistants effectively in daily engineering, and exercise judgement about where they help and where they do not.
- **Operational Stewardship:** Own the operational health, performance, and reliability telemetry of your services in production.
- **Cross-Functional Partnership & Collaboration:** Partner closely with Product, Design, Security, and the other team's engineers to design and validate solutions before implementation begins.

**WHAT YOU BRING TO BITWARDEN**

- **Overall Experience:** 5+ years building and operating production software, with a track record of owning substantial, technically demanding features end to end as an individual contributor.
- **Technical Stack - Expertise:**

  - Languages such as Rust, Go, and Python
  - Tooling such as Terraform, Ansible, and GitHub Actions
  - Containerized environments such as Kubernetes
  - Writing, consuming, and using SDKs / APIs
- **Technical Stack - Experience**:

  - C# / .NET
  - TypeScript / Angular
  - Entity Framework with implementations of Postgres, MySQL, and SQLite
- **Technical Stack - Familiarity:**

  - Languages such as C++, Java, PHP
  - WASM instruction format
- **T-Shaped Engineering Mindset:** Practical experience with containerized environments (Docker/Kubernetes), automated test frameworks (unit, integration, and end-to-end), and SRE/observability tools (APM, alerting, and telemetry dashboards).
- **Secure Coding:** Familiarity with zero-trust and zero-knowledge security architectures, encryption standards, and threat-modeling methodologies.
- **AI-Assisted Development**: Practical experience using AI coding assistants in day-to-day engineering, such as Claude Code, Copilot, or similar.
- **Collaborative Spirit:** A highly collaborative and adaptable mindset, excited to work in rapid, outcome-driven feedback loops.
- **Open Source Passion:** Excitement and enthusiasm for open source, developer advocacy, and building a more secure internet.
- **Problem-Solving:** Excellent problem-solving skills, valuing written, clear documentation and using data to make technical decisions.

#### **Why Join Us?**

- Our user community loves us and we love them. Come to work each day with a sense of purpose as we bring a more secure internet experience to everyone from our friends and family to the world’s largest organizations.
- Become an expert. You’ll get immersed in the prominent technology markets of security and open source software.
- We are dedicated to building a diverse and talented team. Work remotely with motivated and supportive team members across the world.
- Learn and grow. Take on new challenges with the support of your team, and join our #growth-club to continue personal and professional development.

### **Equal Opportunity Employer**

We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can do their best work. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and make employment decisions based on skills, experience, qualifications, and business needs.

**If you enjoy being hands-on, solving hard engineering problems, and having a genuine influence on how products are built, we'd love to hear from you.**
